newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes down, SPT anounces stock split.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes down, SPT anounces stock split.

text.p: Czech shares edged slightly lower in thin-to-moderate trading on Friday with dealers saying the highlight of the day was the announcement of a 10 to one stock split for SPT Telecom.
The PX50 index fell 0.8 percent to 506.4 and the major issue dominated RPIX lost 0.2 percent to 1,057.

Referring to the stock split, whose date has yet to be agreed with the Prague bourse, ING Baring's Lubomir Vystavel said: "This could probably increase the liquidity in the stock which is one of the three most liquid stocks anyway."

On the day, SPT was unchanged on 3,415. The company had its annual general meeting on Friday where it said there would be no further tariff hikes in 1997 and, as expected, confirmed that no dividend would be paid in 1997 or in the foreseeable future.
Elsewhere, Komercni Banka lost more ground, falling 18 crowns to 1,907. Ceska Sporitelna, the second most heavily capitalised banking share after Komercni, fell one crown to 299.
